intro.en: A B2 text to read in one go. Follow the connectors, and notice what triggers each subjunctive.

titulo.en: How to read a B2 text

texto.en:
Before you look up a word, find the **connectors**. They are the skeleton of the argument.

- **No cabe duda de que**: the writer accepts a fact.
- **Sin embargo**: the turn. Here comes the problem.
- **Además**: one more point on the same side.
- **De ahí que**: the consequence.
- **En definitiva**: the conclusion.

Then look at each **subjunctive** and ask what triggered it: **se quejan de que**, **de ahí que**, **proponen que**, **por** pequeña **que**, **para que**.

Finally, guess unknown words from their parts: **masificado** comes from masa; **convivir** is con + vivir.

titulo.en: Tourism: a blessing or a problem?

frases.es: España recibe cada año más de ochenta millones de turistas.
frases.en: Spain receives more than eighty million tourists every year.
analisis: más de ochenta millones de turistas

frases.es: No cabe duda de que el turismo genera ingresos y puestos de trabajo.
frases.en: There is no doubt that tourism generates income and jobs.

frases.es: Sin embargo, en algunas ciudades los vecinos se quejan de que el centro esté masificado.
frases.en: However, in some cities residents complain that the centre is overcrowded.

frases.es: Los alquileres turísticos han subido tanto los precios que muchos jóvenes han tenido que irse del casco antiguo.
frases.en: Holiday lets have pushed prices up so much that many young people have had to leave the old town.

frases.es: Además, el comercio tradicional desaparece a medida que abren tiendas de recuerdos.
frases.en: In addition, traditional shops disappear as souvenir shops open.

frases.es: De ahí que varios ayuntamientos hayan decidido limitar el número de pisos turísticos.
frases.en: Hence several councils have decided to limit the number of tourist flats.

frases.es: Otros proponen que los visitantes paguen una tasa, por pequeña que sea.
frases.en: Others propose that visitors pay a tax, however small it may be.

frases.es: En definitiva, el reto es encontrar un equilibrio para que turistas y vecinos puedan convivir.
frases.en: All in all, the challenge is to find a balance so that tourists and residents can live side by side.

pregunta.en: According to the text, what is the benefit of tourism?

It creates income and jobs.en: Genera ingresos y puestos de trabajo.

It lowers rents.en: The text says prices have gone up.

It protects traditional shops.en: The text says they are disappearing.

pregunta.en: Why have many young people left the old town?

Holiday lets have pushed prices up.en: Han subido tanto los precios que…

There are no jobs there.en: The text does not say that.

The souvenir shops are too noisy.en: The text does not say that.

bloques.correcta: Holiday lets have pushed prices up

To limit the number of tourist flats.en: Limitar el número de pisos turísticos.

To ban tourists from the centre.en: The text does not go that far.

To build more hotels.en: The text does not mention hotels.

bloques.correcta: To limit the number of tourist flats

pregunta.en: Why is «hayan decidido» in the subjunctive?

It follows de ahí que.en: De ahí que always takes the subjunctive.

It is in the past.en: The past alone does not call for the subjunctive.

pregunta.en: Complete: residents complain that the centre is overcrowded.

bloques.frase: Los vecinos se quejan ___ que el centro esté masificado.

explicacion.en: That would be porque es pequeña.
The phrase is a concession about size.

bloques.frase: El reto es encontrar un equilibrio

traduccion.en: The challenge is to find a balance.

texto.en:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write an opinion essay on mass tourism in cities: benefits, problems and solutions.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Give a three-minute talk for or against limiting the number of tourists in historic centres.
